title: Staggered backoff repro notes - 401/429 cascade
content:
Summary:
I observed a reproducible cascade of 401 -> client retry -> concentrated burst of requests -> 429s across several clients after ephemeral key rotation and a brief clock skew. This doc captures the commands I used, observed responses, timing windows, hypotheses and a small test matrix to validate mitigation strategies (staggered backoff, jitter, stricter client-side token refresh gating).

Goal:
- Reproduce the 401/429 pattern deterministically in staging
- Determine whether the server-side quota window or the auth cache is causing the amplification
- Exercise countermeasures (staggered refresh, exponential backoff + jitter, short token grace)

Observed sequence (short):
- 2025-11-03T09:14:12Z client A requests with ephemeral key that has TTL ~2m (rotated by service B) -> returns 401 Unauthorized (token not valid yet according to server)
- client A immediately retries (no backoff), gets 401 again, then re-fetches token and replays queued requests within 2s
- within next 20s, ~150 clients retrying clustered produce 429s from rate limiter (per-key and per-tenant windows)
- server logs show auth service returned "invalid_token" for some requests and "token_expired" for others; cluster of 401s correlates with rotation timestamp

Key hypothesis: competing effects
1) Ephemeral key rotation creates a short window where some tokens are invalidated or not yet propagated to edge auth caches -> everyone retries immediately -> bursts -> 429s
2) Client SDKs lack jitter and use naive immediate retry leading to synchronized spikes
3) Rate limiter buckets are sized so that a small burst exceeds per-key burst capacity but not long-term quota, producing 429s that then cause further retries and a feedback loop

Commands and snippets I ran (staging env, tokens redacted):
- Basic curl to repro 401 (timestamped):
  curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $EPHEMERAL" https://staging.api.rw-inference.com/v1/generate -o /tmp/out.txt 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p'
  -> HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
  Response body: {"error":"invalid_token","message":"token not found in auth-cache"}

- Immediate retry script (Python pseudo):
  import requests
  r = requests.get(url, headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer '+token})
  if r.status_code == 401:
      r2 = requests.get(url, headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer '+token})
  print(r.status_code, r.json())

- Mass repro (GNU parallel) to simulate 200 parallel clients hitting same key within 30s:
  seq 1 200 | parallel -j200 'curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $EPHEMERAL" https://staging.api.../v1/generate -w "%{http_code}\n" -o /dev/null' | sort | uniq -c
  -> observed distribution: 40x 200, 110x 401, 50x 429 (numbers vary by run)

- Instrumented test with staggered backoff (bash):
  for i in $(seq 1 200); do (sleep $(python -c "import random; print(random.random()*4)"); curl ... ) & done
  -> 200s run: 160x 200, 30x 401, 10x 429 (much improved)

Server-side logs sample (redacted):
- auth-proxy-1 [2025-11-03T09:14:12Z] token_check key=ephemeral:x123 status=not_found
- gateway-7  [2025-11-03T09:14:13Z] request_id=... status=401 auth_err=invalid_token
- gateway-7  [2025-11-03T09:14:13Z] rate_limiter key=tenant:acme window=1s used=125 limit=100 action=429
- auth-proxy-2 [2025-11-03T09:14:14Z] token_check key=ephemeral:x123 status=ok cache_populated=true

What I've tried so far (notes):
- Introduced client jitter (random 0-4s) dramatically reduces 429 incidence in staged repros
- Added server-side small grace window: accept tokens with "not_before" up to -2s clock skew; this eliminated many 401s but created edge cases where truly stale tokens accepted (risk: replay?). Need security review
- Adjusted rate limiter burst size to allow higher ephemeral bursts (temporary) — mitigates 429 but hides underlying auth propagation problem
- Instrumented auth cache to emit metrics on miss/hit ratio per rotation event; confirmed miss spike aligned with rotation time

Open questions / unknowns:
- How much of propagation delay is network vs cache warmup? (auth service publishes rotation event to N nodes via pubsub; slow consumer could lag)
- Is there any client that aggressively retries without exponential backoff/jitter in production? We have older SDK versions that do naive immediate retry — need to scan telemetry for client library versions around event times
- Are 429s caused primarily by per-key bucket bursting or per-tenant global bucket? Logs show tenant bucket saturation but also per-key enforcement in some hosts

Next tests to run (prioritized):
1) Controlled rotation with visibility: rotate ephemeral key manually while tailing auth-cache metrics and gateway rate_limiter counters; run traffic with/without jittered clients; measure delta. (Ticket: INFR-4123)
2) Run a variant where client SDK delays refresh gating: if token refresh in-flight, queue outgoing requests for up to 500ms instead of immediate parallel token fetches (simulate with test harness)
3) Binary search to determine minimal stagger/jitter distribution that reduces 429s under given client concurrency (scripts in /staging/scripts)
4) Validate clock sync as contributor: intentionally vary NTP by +-3s on 2 nodes and observe authentication behavior (safest in isolated staging cluster)

Mitigation options (short/medium/long term):
- Short: advise clients to adopt jittered retries; bump rate-limiter temporary burst cap for affected tenants during rotation windows
- Medium: server-side accept small "not_before" skew or implement token pre-warm propagation (publish new token to cache before rotation cutover)
- Long: change rotation workflow to multi-step: publish next token to caches, wait for ack, then switch active token; or implement per-client refresh token flow to avoid single ephemeral token mass rotation

Checklist for experiment run (copy this when doing the test):
- [ ] Schedule staging rotation for 09:00 UTC (notify infra channel)
- [ ] Tail auth-cache hits/misses (prometheus: auth_cache_miss_total)
- [ ] Tail gateway rate limiter metrics (prometheus: rate_limiter_{tenant}_used)
- [ ] Run naive mass-retry script (baseline)
- [ ] Run jittered client script (compare)
- [ ] Collect logs from auth-proxy and gateway nodes (store under /tmp/rotation-test-YYYYMMDD)
- [ ] Post results to Linear ticket INFR-4123 and summary to slack #infra-ops

Notes to self (random):
- Remember to check SRE runbook for key-rotation steps; we may be violating recommended pre-warm
- Ask SDK team about versions older than 1.4 that do immediate retry; make a short compatibility note
- Consider adding a small built-in client helper: TokenRefreshMutex that serializes refresh per-client instance

Raw paste of one failing exchange (for records):
Request: POST /v1/generate Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral:x123>
Response 401 {"error":"invalid_token","desc":"token not found in cache"}
Request (retry 1s later): POST /v1/generate Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral:x123>
Response 429 {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":2}

If anyone picks this up: start by reproducing with the minimal parallel client script and then toggle one mitigation at a time (jitter -> rate-limiter bump -> cache pre-warm). Keep runs labeled by timestamp.

-- Jordan
